public_rationale: The categorical claim that generative AI had peaked is contradicted by independently verified capability gains after August 2024. ARC Prize's December 2025 analysis supplies the decisive event under the stated rule. This is a limited contradiction: it does not establish that generative AI is commercially sustainable, socially worthwhile or destined to fulfill every promise. Those parts remain unsettled.
limitations: The assessment treats reasoning and refinement built around generative models as part of pursuing generative AI.
Benchmark improvements have limits involving task coverage, compute budgets and possible overfitting.
The composite sentence contains broader claims that this evidence does not resolve.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI is a dead-end technology that has peaked, costs too much to sustain, and will not deliver the promises of AI.

statement.excerpt: The promises of artificial intelligence will not be kept through the pursuit of generative AI, as generative AI is a dead-end technology that has peaked, one that costs too much — both financially and socially — to keep it going.

our_interpretation: The categorical peak assertion implies that meaningful further capability advances will not occur after publication.
Substantial, independently measured gains on comparable tasks can falsify that ceiling without proving that all AI promises will be fulfilled.
Generative models used with reasoning, tools or refinement remain within the ordinary scope of pursuing generative AI.
The unspecified promises and financial and social sustainability assertions remain separate limitations on the breadth of any conclusion.
criteria.support_condition: Decisive evidence establishes a lasting technological ceiling and ultimate failure of the identified pursuit. A temporary plateau or current losses alone are insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent, reproducible evaluations demonstrate substantial post-publication capability gains in generative-AI-based systems, falsifying the categorical peak component.

evidence.explanation: The benchmark operator reports verified scores of 37.6% for Opus 4.5 and 54% for a Gemini-based refinement, alongside disclosed methods and open-source solutions. These material advances contradict a categorical capability ceiling, while the report also identifies costs, narrow task coverage and possible overfitting.

evidence.explanation: The earlier evaluation establishes how difficult ARC-AGI-2 remained for o3 and supplies context for the later gains. It also cautions against treating progress as general intelligence or universal reliability.

METR reports a roughly 55-minute task horizon at 50% success for Claude 3.7 Sonnet. This corroborates continuing capability development, but overlapping uncertainty intervals and preliminary testing make it insufficient by itself for decisive resolution.
